papers.title: Degenerate McKean--Vlasov SDE with Yamada--Osgood Coefficients and Arbitrary Modulus of Continuity in Wasserstein Distance
papers.summary: We establish the well-posedness of strong solutions for a class of degenerate mean-field stochastic differential equations with coefficients satisfying non-Lipschitz conditions. The diffusion coefficient is not required to be non-degenerate. Both the diffusion and the drift coefficients may depend on the law through the Kantorovich-Rubinstein metric with an arbitrary modulus of continuity. The drift and the diffusion satisfy a dimension-dependent Osgood-type condition, that becomes particularly sharp in dimension one. The proof combines the classical Yamada--Watanabe argument with Schauder's fixed-point theorem and does not rely on Gaussian estimates, allowing us to cover degenerate diffusions where such estimates are not available. This fills a gap in the existing literature.

papers.title: Factoriality of Mixed $q$-Gaussian Algebras at the Boundary
papers.summary: We determine the center and characterize factoriality for mixed $q$-Gaussian von Neumann algebras associated with real symmetric matrices $Q=(q_{ij})_{i,j\in I}$ satisfying $|q_{ij}|\le1$. We prove that every central element is supported on the singleton components of the strict graph of $Q$ and on its two-vertex components $\{a,b\}$ with $q_{aa}=q_{bb}=-1$ in terms of the graph-theoretic language. We also determine the spectral laws of some central elements.

papers.title: Exact Selective Inference for Spectral Clustering via Piecewise-Constant Graph Perturbation
papers.summary: Cluster labels are often used twice: first to discover groups, and then to test whether the discovered groups differ. This double use of the data makes ordinary two-sample $p$-values anti-conservative. Selective inference fixes this by conditioning on the clustering event, but for spectral clustering the event appears difficult because the algorithm combines an affinity map, an eigendecomposition, and a rounding step. We show that, for spectral clustering based on unweighted $\varepsilon$- or $k$-nearest-neighbor graphs, the obstruction is the affinity construction rather than the eigendecomposition. Along the one-dimensional perturbation used by the truncated-$χ$ selective test, graph changes occur only at finitely many real roots of data-dependent quadratic distance comparisons. Between these breakpoints, the graph, Laplacian spectrum, embedding, rounding, and reported cluster pair are deterministic functions of a finite graph state. Consequently, in real arithmetic and under a known-scale spherical Gaussian model, the selection set is an exact finite union of intervals, yielding finite-sample selective $p$-values for selected spectral-cluster pairs. papers.title: Optical Ceiling on Polaron Mobility in Disordered Molecular Semiconductors: Lessons from Eumelanin
papers.summary: Polaron hopping in disordered molecular semiconductors such as eumelanin is set by energetic disorder $σ$ and reorganization energy $λ$. We show that the reduced polaron absorption band encodes this transport problem. Its value at zero energy fixes the mean hop rate, which bounds the mobility in any dimension. For Gaussian disorder and classical vibrations its centroid is $E_\mathrm{op}=λ+(1-c)σ^2/k_BT$, its variance obeys the Hush relation, and the bound is the Marcus rate at $λ\to E_\mathrm{op}$; a 1D lower bound vanishes at $k_BT^*=(1-c)σ^2/λ$, read from optics.

papers.title: The ALMA survey to Resolve exoKuiper belt Substructures (ARKS) XII. Constraints on large bodies embedded in discs
papers.summary: The ALMA survey to Resolve exoKuiper belt Substructures (ARKS) presents detailed constraints on structure and properties of a sample of 24 debris discs at millimetre wavelengths, including measurements of vertical thicknesses for a subsample of discs. We estimated sizes and total masses of large bodies that feed collisional cascades producing the observed millimetre dust in 11 ARKS discs with a well constrained vertical thickness. Separately, we estimated the sizes and total masses of large bodies that could be gravitationally stirring these discs, assuming that such stirring is the origin of the vertical thickness. We used a semi-analytic particle-in-a-box collisional model and a semi-analytic model of stirring through gravitational scattering. We accounted for the dependence of collisional damping efficiency on the average collision velocity. We find that planetesimals feeding the collisional cascades are less than 20 km in size, while the total masses in the planetesimals are lower than 200 M$_\oplus$. There is a good agreement between minimum disc masses inferred from millimetre and infrared observations. The hypothetical stirrers are always larger in size than the planetesimal

papers.title: A Bayesian Optimized Biquad Filter-Burg Model for Real-Time EEG Phase Estimation
papers.summary: Real-time phase estimation on stimulus-aligned transient EEG is critical for closed-loop neuromodulation systems targeting the theta-band, yet most real-time phase estimation methods have been developed and validated on resting-state, high-fidelity signals in the alpha band. Recent work has pursued deep learning architectures, while individualized classical bandpass filter tuning remains underexplored. This study characterizes the spectral and temporal properties of non-anticipative bandpass filtering and demonstrates the performance gains achieved through individualized tuning. We present a Bayesian-Optimized Biquad Filter-Burg (BOB) model evaluated on EEG recorded during peripheral vibrotactile stimulation of the left median nerve (theta, N=20 healthy subjects) and on resting-state recordings from the Max Planck Institute's LEMON dataset (alpha, N=20 healthy subjects). BOB was benchmarked against the Deep Dual-Branch Complex Neural Network (DBCNN), EEG Phase Prediction Network (EPN), Phastimate, and Phase Estimation with Autoregressive Padding (PEAP) under matched testing conditions: channel selection, individualized optimization, evaluation time points, and an offline reference

papers.title: Higher-order interactions renormalize the thermodynamic signature of neural population codes
papers.summary: Maximum-entropy models of neural recordings can be treated as Boltzmann distributions at a fictitious temperature $T$, with the fitted model at $T=1$. Their specific-heat peak grows with population size and approaches that temperature, which has been read as a sign of criticality. The case rests on pairwise models, yet retinal codes require higher-order interactions. The thermodynamics of a model with such interactions fitted cell by cell has not been computed. Here I compute it exactly for pairwise and third-order models of the same populations of up to $20$ retinal ganglion cells, in salamander and marmoset. The triplet terms, required by the held-out likelihood, shift the peak by more than the finite-sample bias, with opposite sign in the two retinas. The peak is lower and grows more slowly in salamander, higher and grows faster in marmoset, and lies closer to $T=1$ in both. An exact decomposition traces most of the shift to the energy variance across population spike counts. A constraint on the spike-count distribution alone reproduces all of it in salamander and over half in marmoset. papers.title: Reality and Perceptual Gaps in Expressive Swarm Robotics
papers.summary: Moving robot swarms from simulation into the physical world can be difficult because small discrepancies in hardware, timing and communication can cascade across interacting robots and alter group behaviour. This challenge is known as the reality gap. When swarms operate in human environments, a second challenge emerges: a perceptual gap between what the swarm physically does and what human onlookers actually perceive. This study examines the same decentralised coordination code deployed across three robotic swarms-tabletop, aerial and human-scale mobile manipulators-during live artistic performances. We find that while the underlying algorithms executed reliably on all three platforms, physical embodiment drastically altered visible motion-distorting execution timescales by more than a factor of three and reshaping trajectory geometry. More importantly, audience surveys revealed that human interpretation does not mirror technical success: how observers attribute meaning (perceived purpose) and how they react emotionally (comfort versus threat) depend heavily on physical form. papers.title: Label-Preserving Fourier Domain Adaptation with Generative-AI and Real Style Donors for 3D Mitral Valve Segmentation
papers.summary: Accurate segmentation of the mitral valve from three-dimensional transesophageal echocardiography (3D TEE) is severely restricted by the scarcity of publicly available expert- annotated volumetric datasets. To address this critical limitation, we investigated Fourier Domain Adaptation (FDA), utilizing general-purpose generative-AI images (from platforms like Chat- GPT, Google Gemini, and Microsoft MAI) as annotation-free style donors for 3D mitral valve segmentation. We employed a DeepMitral residual U-Net model on the public MVSeg2023 dataset, comparing six conditions over three runs: real-only training, traditional augmentation, FDA with each generative source, and a non-AI FDA control using real-image style donors, plus an optimization-matched real-only control and a \b{eta} sensitivity analysis. Case-level paired testing showed that FDA with these generative sources led to significant reductions in boundary- and surface-related errors across all three donor conditions relative to the primary real-only baseline. However, the impact on the core segmentation metric, Generalized Dice Score (GDS), proved generator-dependent. ChatGPT-FDA showed a significant GDS advantage over the op

papers.title: DRAP: Dynamics-Risk Adaptive Plasticity for Continual Learning in Physical AI
papers.summary: Continual learning in physical AI differs from conventional continual learning because small per-step policy errors can accumulate over a trajectory. Each deviation may move the agent outside the training distribution, increase subsequent prediction errors, and ultimately cause closed-loop task failure. This work introduces Dynamics-Risk Adaptive Plasticity (DRAP), a replay-free method that estimates the historical importance of adaptable model tensors from sample-level action gradients weighted by local trajectory-amplification risk. A ridge-regularized local linear model is fitted to expert state-action transitions, and the largest singular value of its state-transition matrix provides a policy-independent, Lyapunov-inspired estimate of one-step perturbation amplification. After each task, risk-weighted squared gradients are accumulated in a tensor-level importance memory. During subsequent tasks, DRAP uses normalized cumulative importance to scale the effective AdamW learning rate of each tensor, immediately reducing the plasticity of components that supported previous behavior at dynamically sensitive trajectory points. papers.title: A Multidimensional Evaluation Framework for Artificial Intelligence-Based Ocean State Forecasts
papers.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) based ocean state forecasts now approach or surpass those produced by operational ocean forecasting systems as measured by conventional pointwise metrics. However, these metrics may favor spatially smoothed forecasts and cannot determine whether forecast variables remain physically coherent. Forecast evaluation should therefore move beyond overall pointwise accuracy toward assessing forecast trustworthiness. We propose a multidimensional framework comprising overall pointwise accuracy, physical consistency, and distributional consistency. Overall pointwise accuracy summarizes forecast and reference agreement over all valid samples; physical consistency evaluates dynamical balances using model outputs alone; and distributional consistency evaluates distribution tails and multiscale spatial structures. Three AI models were deployed as representative testbeds in a unified operational environment. This comprehensive assessment shows that lower overall pointwise errors cannot preclude substantial dynamical imbalances and suppressed fine-scale variance. papers.title: AI for eGovernance: Leveraging Language Technologies For Digital Inclusion
papers.summary: The Kenyan government has invested heavily in the digitisation of public service delivery, in line with the Kenya Digital Master Plan 2022-2032. The national eGovernment platform, eCitizen, hosts services that are vital to citizens' livelihoods, including business registration, youth enterprise lending, digital literacy and tax filing. However, the platform faces digital inclusion challenges that limit equitable access for marginalised groups, particularly youth in rural areas and persons with disabilities. This exclusion is driven by a language barrier, since the platform is primarily in English with limited Swahili support, and by a text-only interface that excludes low-literacy and visually impaired users. This paper reports findings from six one-on-one interviews and an eleven-person roundtable discussion across four platforms essential to youth livelihoods: Ajira Digital, Kenya Revenue Authority (KRA) iTax, Higher Education Loans Board (HELB) and the Youth Enterprise Development Fund (YEDF). papers.title: AgenticFinBench: Benchmarking Financial Agents on Diverse Tasks from Real-World Requests
papers.summary: Financial agents are becoming an important class of real-world AI systems. Financial tasks vary widely in type and difficulty, and many are open-ended with no ground-truth answers. However, existing benchmarks neither capture this breadth and open-endedness nor separate grounding from correctness. To bridge this gap, we introduce $\textbf{AgenticFinBench}$, a benchmark of 230 real-world financial tasks spanning 8 categories, 2 languages, and 4 complexity levels. We also propose a reference-free evaluation framework that combines question-specific rubrics with a two-stage claim audit that detects hallucinations, defined as claims absent from the agent's trace and refuted by external evidence. This framework better matches how financial work is assessed in practice. Experiments across 18 agent configurations reveal three key findings: (1) Ignoring hallucinations can overstate agent performance: hallucination auditing lowers the baseline leader's score by 7.58 points and moves it to fourth place. papers.title: MDSKILL: Learning to Internalize Skill Memory through Multi-View Distillation for Efficient Dynamic Agent Self-Evolution
papers.summary: Skill memories encode past experiences as textual prompts to improve reinforcement learning (RL) for self-evolving agents. Complementing RL, On-Policy Self-Distillation (OPSD) provides dense, fine-grained supervision to internalize knowledge from skill-guided trajectories and accelerate policy learning. However, self-generated memories often contain noisy supervision and functionally entangled, redundant, or conflicting knowledge, making direct distillation difficult. Under limited training budgets, these issues can hinder knowledge internalization and even degrade performance. To address this problem, we propose MDSKILL, a multi-view distillation approach for skill memory internalization. MDSKILL organizes skill memories into three complementary functional views (state grounding, action planning, and execution control) and selects high-quality skills using dynamic metrics to construct view-specific and integrated reasoning branches. OPSD then transfers and consolidates complementary experiential knowledge across these branches into a shared policy, enabling efficient skill internalization and continuous agent self-evolution. papers.title: GSBR: Geometric Support Behavior Regularization for Online RL
papers.summary: Regularizing online reinforcement learning (RL) toward a pretrained base policy can improve sample efficiency and learning stability, but regularization that is too restrictive limits how much the policy can improve. Base policies -- typically diffusion or flow-matching models trained by imitation learning on large, diverse datasets -- capture many behaviors that are reasonable but suboptimal. Existing regularizers using such base policies are too restrictive in one of two ways: behavioral cloning regularizers pull the actor toward the full base-policy distribution, penalizing it for discarding suboptimal modes, while hard support constraints forbid improvements that lie just outside the base policy's support. We propose Geometric Support Behavior Regularization (GSBR), which penalizes actions by their distance from the base policy's support. Actions within the support incur no penalty, so the actor can concentrate on high-value modes; outside the support, where value estimates are less reliable, the penalty grows smoothly with distance while still permitting improvement when the value gained outweighs the penalty. papers.title: Factorized MLLM Embeddings for Composed Image Retrieval
papers.summary: Composed Image Retrieval (CIR) aims to retrieve a target image given a reference image and a modification text. Although recent approaches leveraging Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have shown significant progress, we argue that the MLLM's compositional understanding remains underutilized. This stems from directly mapping composed queries into a retrieval embedding via contrastive supervision alone, without explicitly resolving the intended visual modifications. In this work, we introduce Factorized MLLM Embeddings (FactEmbed), which decouples compositional query comprehension from building discriminative embeddings. Rather than directly projecting the composed query into a single embedding without internal reasoning, FactEmbed employs a set of factorized latents that simulate the intended visual modifications via an intermediate target imagination objective. This process encourages the latents to ground into target semantics before forming discriminative representations for retrieval. papers.title: From Natural Images to Medical Scans: Transferability of Diffusion Models for Medical Image Generation
papers.summary: Transfer learning from natural images is standard in supervised and increasingly adopted in self-supervised medical image analysis, but its role in generative modelling, and in particular diffusion denoisers, remains underexplored. Medical diffusion models typically train the denoiser from scratch, with no systematic evaluation of natural-image transfer. We analyse this across latent and pixel paradigms, model sizes (131M-952M) and two radiology datasets (RadImageNet, BraTS), and ask which aspects of transfer support generation. papers.title: Analog signal processing, storage, and demultiplexing via in-materia wave-based computing
papers.summary: The ability of mechanical systems to perform basic computations has gained traction in recent years, providing a robust supplement to digital computing in off-grid, low-power, and extreme environments where electronics are inaccessible or risk failure. However, prior work has focused on Boolean logic applied via bistable structures, snap-through mechanisms, or origami lattices. Digital signal processing (DSP) underpins a wide range of computational tasks, providing the foundation for information encoding, manipulation, and analysis. In contrast to conventional DSP approaches, we present a new paradigm for analog information processing, where an elastic substrate houses a spatial wave-based platform for mechanical signal manipulation in the temporal domain. The proposed metasurface-based system exploits temperature-dependent phase transitions of shape memory alloys (SMAs) to realize key signal-processing functionalities, including gating, retention, and programmable delay of impinging mechanical loads. papers.title: The Novelty Horizon H_N: Why Large Language Models Fail to Generate Scientific Data beyond Their Training Distribution
papers.summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) lack physical grounding and extrapolation. This paper formalises the Novelty Horizon as tasks needing extrapolation beyond training support, causal reasoning absent from learned correlations, or post-frontier information. A forensic analysis tests LLMs on unguided, guided, and ground-truth data from an underrepresented diode-clamped short-circuit experiment using temporal, spectral, and statistical validation against a first-principles Modified Ohm's Law. Both script-based approaches fail catastrophically with physical and spectral inconsistencies, extreme statistical pathologies, zero Generative Fidelity Score, and linear-regime outputs. Direct prompting corroborates distinct failure modes. This paper introduces the Past Information Boundary and physics-based authentication. LLM data generation cannot extrapolate past the Novelty Horizon essential for novel discovery. Hybrid neuro-symbolic systems must preserve human causal reasoning and experimental design.

papers.title: Basin2Vec: Learning Basin-Centric Embeddings for Scalable Hydrological Modeling
papers.summary: Reliable streamflow prediction across time and in ungauged basins requires representations that capture hydrologically relevant basin characteristics. Existing methods rely on either fixed handcrafted attributes or general-purpose Earth observation embeddings not tailored to basin structure. We introduce \textbf{Basin2Vec}, a self-supervised framework that learns compact basin representations from hydroclimatic and physiographic data without observed streamflow. Basin2Vec organizes representation learning around basin scale and relationships across space and time. Across multiple forecasting architectures, it consistently outperforms predefined attributes and general-purpose geospatial embeddings in temporal generalization and zero-shot spatial transfer. Basin2Vec provides average relative gains of up to 8.3% temporally and achieves 3.5x the median predictive performance of the strongest baselines on unseen basins. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of basin-centric pretraining for transferable hydrologic prediction. Code is available at https://github.com/Muhammad-Talha-MT/basin2vec

papers.title: High-fidelity training-free photovoltaic module mapping from multi-view UAV imagery
papers.summary: High-fidelity photovoltaic (PV) module mapping requires complete instance recovery and accurate delineation. Vision foundation models offer zero-shot segmentation, but converting incomplete and inconsistent predictions across views into a complete, geometrically accurate map of individual modules remains challenging. We propose the Multi-View PV Module Mapper (MV-PVMapper), a training-free framework coupling vision foundation models with unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) photogrammetry. First, Segment Anything Model 3 (SAM 3) generates candidates from original images using text prompts. Their contours are then transferred into object space through per-module slope correction to limit distortion from surface-model noise, and verified against representative module dimensions to guide cross-view instance selection. Finally, accepted instances return to all covering images as box prompts for SAM~3, supplementing text prompts with spatial cues for iterative segmentation, verification and fusion. papers.title: High-order compact ALE gas-kinetic scheme on three-dimensional unstructured meshes
papers.summary: In this paper, a compact high-order gas-kinetic scheme (HGKS) is developed for compressible arbitrary Lagrangian-Eulerian (ALE) computations on three-dimensional unstructured meshes. To achieve high-order spatial accuracy, a large number of matrix inversions are required for spatial reconstruction. In ALE computations, the mesh moves and the geometric information must be recalculated at each time step, which reduces computational efficiency. To improve efficiency, a memory-reduction reconstruction strategy is employed to construct a quadratic polynomial on unstructured meshes. By differentiating the candidate polynomial, the quadratic terms are obtained by the least-squares method using the average gradient values of the cell itself and its neighboring cells. The linear terms of the polynomial are also determined by the least-squares method. On three-dimensional unstructured meshes, a $3\times3$ coefficient matrix must be stored, and four least-squares procedures are required to construct a quadratic polynomial. papers.title: LoopQ: Fair, Closed-Loop Evaluation of Quantized Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.summary: Post-training quantization (PTQ) for vision-language-action (VLA) models promises smaller and faster VLA deployments. However, when analyzing existing VLA quantization works, we realised that it is hard to reason about the performance of the suggested quantization method compared to existing, similar, or in many cases, simpler PTQ methods. We present LoopQ, a closed-loop benchmark that compares multiple quantization policies on the same checkpoint, layers and engine, varying only the method and the kernels. We evaluate RTN, AWQ, GPTQ, ActQuant and QuantVLA on four VLAs with more than 180,000 episodes of LIBERO and LIBERO-plus, compare against QVLA's reported results on the same layers, and benchmark whether the four public VLA-quantization releases can be reproduced. We benchmark the methods on an NVIDIA H100, an L4, and a Jetson AGX Thor. Our results show that while quantization reliably saves memory, 2-3x for real low-bit models, VLA-specific PTQ methods underperform compared to simpler generic baselines. papers.title: Designing tunable hyperuniformity in random organization through nonlocal noise
papers.summary: Hyperuniform fluids suppress density fluctuations at large length scales, but microscopic protocols for designing their asymptotic scaling remain limited. Here we show how effective driving noise generated by particle dynamics can select the hyperuniform exponent while preserving ordinary diffusion and pairwise center-of-mass conservation of the organized particles. papers.title: Möbius: A Unified Motion-Language Model Bridging Understanding and Generation
papers.summary: We aim to build a truly unified motion model that can understand, generate, and edit human motion within a single framework. Existing motion UMMs remain only partially unified: motion understanding is handled by a language model, while generation is often delegated to a separate diffusion module operating over learned motion latents. We introduce Möbius, which brings the entire diffusion process into the same multimodal representation space used for motion understanding. Clean motion, noisy motion, and text jointly participate in shared attention, while role-specific parameters process understanding and generation streams. Importantly, Möbius operates directly on continuous frame-level raw motion, requiring neither discrete tokenization nor a pretrained motion VAE. This simple formulation naturally supports motion captioning, text-to-motion generation, temporal completion, and instruction-guided editing within a single model. On HumanML3D, Möbius achieves state-of-the-art performance among unified motion models. Scaling to 1.7B parameters and 1,700 hours of motion data further demonstrates that our framework is both effective and scalable.

papers.title: De Rham cohomological architectures for PINNs and PDEs with topological holes
papers.summary: We attempt to alleviate failure modes of classical physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) in scenarios of topological pathologies corresponding to punctures, holes, poles, and voids by introducing de Rham cohomological augmentations, or Hodge-de Rham PINNs. papers.title: Learning Behaviorally Relevant Dynamics in Multimodal Neural Recordings
papers.summary: Multimodal neural data can enable a more complete understanding of brain dynamics underlying behavior. Modalities such as spiking activity, local field potentials (LFPs), and behavior capture diverse spatiotemporal aspects of brain processes, yet prior neural-behavioral models that separate sources of variability rely on a single neural modality. By leveraging these complementary strengths, multimodal neural fusion can provide a unified, rich representation of brain-behavior processes and address the limitations of single-modality analyses. Here we develop BREM-NET, a nonlinear multimodal dynamical model that integrates behavior with multiple neural modalities having distinct statistical characteristics and temporal resolutions. BREM-NET performs multimodal neural fusion during inference while separating behaviorally relevant and residual neural dynamics via a structured learning framework. papers.title: Perturb, Repair, Verify: Self-Play Vision-Language Verifiers for Compositional Understanding
papers.summary: Vision-language verifiers judge whether an image faithfully matches a textual description, yet existing training pipelines typically rely on static supervision from stronger external judges or curated hard-negative data. Such supervision requires external generation or annotation, is teacher-bounded, and is difficult to adapt as model failures evolve. We introduce PROVE (Perturb-and-Repair Optimization for Vision-Language Evaluation), a self-play framework that trains verifiers through a closed perturb-verify-repair-verify loop. Starting from a known-correct image-caption pair, a Mutator introduces a typed perturbation over objects, attributes, counts, or relations. The verifier then judges the perturbed caption and provides textual feedback, which a Repairer uses to recover a faithful caption for re-verification. These two verification rounds produce structured rewards for informative mismatches and visually grounded repairs. Since perturbation, verification, and repair are role-conditioned behaviors of the same evolving multimodal backbone, updating the shared parameters also improves the verifier itself. papers.summary: Channel estimators at a newly deployed base station usually start from 3GPP stochastic channel models, which describe no particular street. We ask whether a channel prior pooled from many ray-traced cities serves an unseen site better than the 3GPP CDL models, and whether learned estimators make the difference. Learned models added little: at most 0.65 dB in estimation, and in channel prediction a simple classical method beat CNN predictors by 1.8-12 dB from 2 ms ahead. papers.summary: Speech large language models retain audio history to support multi-turn conversations. Yet remembering an event does not ensure that its information is used only when relevant. We investigate why irrelevant historical audio changes answers even when the queried event remains represented. Controlled experiments on MOSS-Audio and MiMo-Audio show that historical values direct errors toward specific competing answers, beyond a generic effect of context length. Causal interventions distinguish two paths. In open-ended question answering, most history-value errors disappear when subsequent computation cannot directly access the irrelevant source. In multiple-choice answering, many errors persist: early historical influence is carried by question-candidate states even after direct source access is blocked. Low-dimensional interventions further separate source-role information from answer-value information. papers.title: HLO-AMP: Hierarchical Loco-Manipulation from Object-Aware Motion Priors
papers.summary: Hierarchical pipelines for humanoid loco-manipulation typically pair a task-agnostic whole-body controller (WBC) with a downstream task policy. Such WBCs are often trained through manual reward shaping, which yields visibly machine-like motions; more consequentially, they are trained without the manipulated object in the scene. Object dynamics are instead approximated through randomized end-effector force disturbances, a proxy that fails to reproduce the distributed multi-contact wrench a real payload applies across the arms and torso, with the gap becoming critical near the platform's payload limit. In this work, we train the low-level (LL) controller itself as an object-aware motion prior: a single policy trained via motion imitation on retargeted motion-capture (MoCap) references that span the core motion primitives of the downstream task, with the manipulated object physically present in the scene. This single stage inherits natural human-like coordination from the references and absorbs the realistic contact wrench at its source, while exposing the same compact task-space command interface used by command-tracking WBCs. papers.title: Lightweight graph transformers for clutter and target classification in automotive radar
papers.summary: Radar is a core sensor modality for scene perception to achieve higher levels of autonomy in automotive driving. A common occurrence in automotive radars is clutter - detections of non-existent moving objects, that can adversely impact target detection and classification performance and subsequent driving actions. We propose lightweight tiny graph transformer network (TGTNet) models for classifying clutter from stationary and moving targets in the scene. Performance evaluation on the public RadarScenes show that our proposed TGTNet models achieve similar classification performance in precision and recall metrics in comparison to state of the art models, with one to two orders of magnitude lower model size and significantly faster inference.

papers.title: Field-free transverse response in altermagnet and topological insulator heterojunctions
papers.summary: We theoretically investigate the transport properties of a topological insulator (TI) connected to two-dimensional altermagnetic (AM) leads in the absence of an external magnetic field. Exploiting the intrinsic time-reversal symmetry breaking of altermagnets, we report the emergence of a field-free transverse differential conductivity in the resulting AM-TI-AM heterostructure. Our analysis reveals that this transverse response is highly sensitive to the orientation of the Néel vector: a finite transverse conductivity manifests when the Néel vector possesses an out-of-plane component, whereas it strictly vanishes for in-plane orientations ($θ= π/2$) under symmetric chemical potentials ($μ_t = μ_b$) due to the restoration of symmetry between the $k_y$ and $-k_y$ momentum channels. Conversely, when asymmetric chemical potentials are applied ($μ_t \neq μ_b$), this symmetry is broken, yielding a finite transverse response even for an in-plane Néel vector. papers.title: Behind Video Generation: Observations and Insights on Multimodal Understanding from Kling
papers.summary: Video generation has progressed from isolated clips to coherent short-form audiovisual sequences, and the bottleneck is shifting from rendering to semantic control. This report summarizes the observations and insights on multimodal understanding gained from successive generations of Kling. We argue that generation quality is the projection of multimodal understanding through the entire data--conditioning--alignment--evaluation chain, and we examine this chain module by module. Kling-MLLM, a shared multimodal foundation model that unifies image, video, audio, synchronized audio--video, and interleaved inputs, is specialized for each downstream module. Because a DiT is trained on far fewer training samples than a language model, we treat captioning as a semantic contract that maximizes description density, and extend it to reference-grounded captioning that makes reference bindings explicit. Prompt enhancement translates user intent into this caption distribution: basic PE is derived from captions of compelling videos and refined with text-level and generator-in-the-loop reinforcement learning, while agentic PE refines the story and retrieves compelling examples. papers.title: Aligning Language Models with General Preferences: An Empirical Study of Direct Nash Optimization
papers.summary: Direct Nash Optimization (DNO) aligns a language model to a general preference function by approximating the Nash equilibrium of a two-player preference game. Its practical variant, DNO-Prct, iterates on-policy sampling, LLM-based rating of the samples together with a teacher's gold response, large-margin preference-pair selection and a DPO-style contrastive update. We re-implement DNO-Prct independently and study it on two open-weight instruct models, Llama 3.1 8B Instruct and Mistral 7B Instruct v0.1, with GPT-4o or a larger open-weight model of the same family as the annotator. On AlpacaEval 2.0 with GPT-4o as judge, three iterations raise the length-controlled (LC) win rate against GPT-4o from 31.7% to 45.3% for Llama and from 6.8% to 18.4% for Mistral, and the tuned 8B model scores above Llama 3.1 70B Instruct on every reported win rate. With same-family open-weight annotators, the runs retain 62% (Llama) and 82% (Mistral) of the LC gain achieved with GPT-4o as annotator, so the rating step does not require a proprietary model. papers.title: Suppressing Misaligned Behaviors in Language Models, Durably
papers.summary: Undesired model behaviors can emerge or re-emerge at any stage of training. Once observed, how effectively can we suppress them? To study this question, we first construct two model organisms--language models deliberately trained to exhibit a specific misalignment--that differ in what triggers the behavior. The narrow-trigger organism misbehaves only when the prompt contains a specific cue: it cheats on multiple-choice questions by following a planted hint that points to a wrong answer, and behaves normally otherwise. The broad-trigger organism has no such cue: after fine-tuning on insecure code, it gives harmful responses across a wide range of open-ended prompts. We then formalize post-hoc behavioral suppression and evaluate methods along three criteria: immediate suppression of the target behavior, durability under further training, and preservation of general capability. We compare standard methods--SFT, GRPO, and gradient-ascent unlearning--along these dimensions. Building on prior work on alignment shallowness, we hypothesize that more durable suppression requires the ability to recover from a wider range of misalignment states. papers.title: MedPhysBench: A Benchmark for Evaluating Language Models on Medical Physics Calculations and Error Detection
papers.summary: Medical physicists turn a prescription into a delivered dose and check one another's calculations, because one error in a beam calibration or a monitor-unit (MU) calculation can affect every patient treated with it. MedPhysBench has ten seeded generators of calculation items in radiation therapy, diagnostic imaging, nuclear medicine and radiation protection, up to clinical tasks such as a TG-51 calibration worksheet. Reference answers come from code implementing the governing protocols, and a grader converts units and applies tolerance bands. From the same inputs, separate checking items test error detection, showing a colleague's worksheet or only the colleague's result, half correct and half with one planted error. On a held-out test split of 1,200 items (half for two models), 12 models scored 33.3 to 100.0% on calculation. Of the nine answers graded incorrect for the four best (99.3-100.0%), five contained model errors and four followed NCRP Report 151 on points our items misstate or leave open. papers.title: A simple adaptive accelerated optimistic dual averaging method for unconstrained convex optimization in $p$-norm geometry
papers.summary: Efficient preconditioning plays an important role in large-scale first-order optimization. In this paper, we propose an adaptive accelerated optimistic dual averaging ($\text{A}^2$ODA) method for unconstrained convex optimization that adopts low-cost preconditioning based on $p$-norm geometry for $p\in[2,\infty]$. The method is line-search-free and employs a new stepsize selection technique based on an aggregated affine lower model. Its update structure is simple and unified across $p\in[2,\infty]$, with the case $p>2$ requiring no more elaborate updates than the Euclidean case $p=2$. Under a generalized local smoothness condition, we derive a convergence bound that separates the effects of constant and gap-dependent curvature, with the latter potentially yielding faster-decaying terms. In the special case of local smoothness, this bound recovers a nearly optimal convergence rate.

papers.title: HARP: Training-Free Dual-Profile Agentic Communication for LLM-Based Recommendation
papers.summary: In LLM-based recommendation, memory acts as a user-level agent in a memory-augmented backbone. Yet users and items remain asymmetric: only the user is given a structured profile; it enters a bandwidth-limited reranker prompt; and it is frozen after warmup. We recast LLM-based recommendation as an agentic-communication process in four stages: BUILD a self-description, TRANSMIT it along the collaborative graph, UNDERSTAND the other side, and SYNC it from the next interaction. This formulation reveals three unresolved communication challenges: the item side never produces a comparable self-description (one-sided BUILD); profile-level signals enter only the bandwidth-limited reranker prompt rather than retrieval, where they would not compete for context tokens (prompt-trapped UNDERSTAND); and the user's description is frozen after warmup with no principled update rule (absent SYNC). papers.title: You don't need long context
papers.summary: Later tokens are costlier to generate than earlier tokens. On frontier open weight models, the disparity in cost may rise to as much as 7x. Through frequent compaction, we show across a broad range of long-horizon and long-input tasks that frontier language models sacrifice little to no task accuracy when maintaining short contexts. We further demonstrate that LLM performance does not collapse on long-horizon software engineering tasks even when taking at most one action per context, and based on that we outline the concept of semantic state space models (SSSMs). Our findings question the need for long-context language models.

papers.title: Personas Are Not People: Identity as State, Not Attribute
papers.summary: Synthetic populations, large sets of simulated people, are increasingly used in place of real people to pretest surveys, simulate users and communities, and evaluate AI systems. Each simulated person is defined by a persona, a written profile of fixed traits, demographics, and attitudes that a language model is instructed to act out. Every such system assumes that a person's identity is a stable attribute that behaves the same way in every situation the simulation presents. We show that this assumption is not a harmless simplification. Three decades of personality research find the opposite. How a given person behaves varies more across contexts than people vary from one another. Drawing on identity economics, which describes how different situations activate different identities and norms within the same person, we separate behavior into three parts, which are stable traits, the identity a context calls up, and the situation itself. We then prove, under two stated assumptions, that any simulation built on fixed personas, no matter how detailed the personas or how large the underlying model, cannot reproduce the part of a population's behavior that is specific to it and its circums

papers.title: False Reassurance in LLM Severe-Weather Guidance: A Replayable Evaluation Against Real NWS Alerts
papers.summary: An LLM assistant that cannot see official severe-weather alerts may tell users that conditions are calm while a warning is active. We call this false reassurance and measure it by replaying 117 frozen cases built from real U.S. National Weather Service (NWS) alerts (69 alert cases, 32 no-alert controls, 16 non-U.S. locations) through five conditions of a Claude-based preparedness pipeline that differ in alert access and prompt design. One rater hand-labeled all 342 alert-case responses under a seven-category scheme written after an initial binary pass, which we disclose. False reassurance was 0.0% for the production pipeline (0/66, 95% CI 0.0-5.5) and for the same alerts under a neutral prompt (0/69), 37.7% for a blind neutral prompt (26/69), and 44.9% when the blind prompt also told the model to disclose its blind spot (31/69). Every case was implicit; no response explicitly denied an alert. Real alerts removed false reassurance (paired McNemar p < 0.0001); the disclosure instruction did not (p = 0.40). papers.title: Knowingly Wrong: Training LLMs Against Their Own Beliefs can Induce Misalignment
papers.summary: Fine-tuning a large language model (LLM) on harmful data in a narrow domain, such as bad medical advice, can make it broadly misaligned. How realistic this risk is remains unclear, since models are very rarely fine-tuned on explicitly harmful data in practice. In this work, we show that fine-tuning on data the model believes to be false but that has no harmful content, can also induce broad misalignment. Across mathematics, trivia, cooking and sports, the more strongly the model disbelieves the answers it is trained on, the more misaligned it becomes. In mathematics, misaligned answers rise from 4% to over 60% as the training answers become more wrong, with little loss of general capability. After fine-tuning, the model states the wrong answers but its multiple-choice probabilities still prefer the true ones, which suggests that misalignment comes from this internal inconsistency. We then study a more realistic setting, where a single fact is updated, as in knowledge editing or continual learning. papers.title: Fairness Metrics based on the AUC in Clinical Predictive AI
papers.summary: Fairness evaluation of clinical prediction models for binary outcomes often involves fairness metrics that compare the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC, or c-statistic) across subgroups. However, the AUC has been shown to be a non-collapsible metric, meaning that its subgroup specific and overall values are not directly comparable as often implicitly assumed. This raises important questions about how existing AUC-based fairness metrics should be used and interpreted. We examine eight AUC-based fairness metrics proposed in the literature, including: within-group AUC parity; cross-group AUC (xAUC) parity; gap-to-overall AUC; equity-scaled AUC; minimum-based metrics; $\mathrm{xAUC}^1$; $\mathrm{xAUC}^0$; and $\mathrm{xAUC}^1$ or $\mathrm{xAUC}^0$ parity. We characterise their estimands, relate them to the decomposition of overall AUC (into within- and cross-group components), and critically appraise them. We then illustrate their behaviour using simulations based on the EuroSCORE II, a clinical prediction model for in-hospital mortality. papers.title: SBi3PCF: cosmology with Dark Energy Survey Year 3 cosmic shear
papers.summary: We present the first cosmic shear data analysis of the integrated 3-point correlation function (i3PCF), a higher-order weak lensing statistic, and the first simulation-based inference (SBI) analysis of a three-point cosmic shear correlation function on survey data. Our forward model is built on the CosmoGridV1 N-body simulations and includes the survey mask, shape noise, intrinsic alignment, baryonic feedback, photometric redshift uncertainty and shear calibration bias. The analysis was carried out blind, with all choices frozen, and only unblinded once coverage tests, tests of the accuracy of the learned likelihoods, and internal consistency tests had been passed. papers.title: A wider state, not wider arithmetic, for single-precision time integration
papers.summary: Single precision (FP32) halves the memory and data movement of double precision (FP64), and on accelerators is often several times faster. Its rounding errors are harmless except in the stored state. A modified equation for Runge-Kutta methods in Shu-Osher form and linear multistep methods separates the rounding of the stored state, a forcing proportional to $1/Δt$, from truncation and from right-hand-side rounding, which sets a $Δt$-independent floor. We bound this forcing for strong-stability-preserving schemes and identify two mechanisms that keep its sign fixed, so it accumulates as a bias: past a turnaround step, refining the step increases the error, in FP64 as in FP32. For a model oscillator the analysis predicts the floor and the FP32-to-FP64 ratios of turnaround step and minimum error within 30%. papers.title: Designing an Adaptive Robust and Evolutionary-Game Framework for Minimum Shipment Quotas in Capacity-Constrained Freight Markets
papers.summary: Minimum shipment quota regulations ensure that socially critical commodities are not excluded from capacity-constrained freight markets by profit-driven allocation. Existing models of such regulation are deterministic and static, assuming perfect market knowledge and instantaneous convergence to a rational equilibrium. This paper relaxes both assumptions through a framework combining adaptive robust optimization, multi-objective optimization, and evolutionary game theory. A robust optimization model first characterizes the regulator's quota-setting problem under uncertain commodity availability, trading social welfare against enforcement cost to generate a Pareto frontier of quota policies. This frontier then defines the regulator's strategy space in a three-population evolutionary game in which the regulator, suppliers, and carrier co-evolve under replicator dynamics, so that the prevailing policy emerges from the interaction of the three players. The framework is calibrated to a Canadian rail freight case study that covers crude oil, corn, barley, and oat. papers.summary: We study cold, electrically neutral, beta-equilibrated quark matter with u, d, and s quarks described by a symmetry-preserving contact interaction whose parameters are fixed in vacuum. The vector repulsion is varied as a fraction 0 < eta < 3/2 of the scalar coupling, and results are given with and without the flavor dressing of the effective coupling. Pure quark matter is not self-bound in this model, and no value of eta produces a star that reaches two solar masses while satisfying the tidal constraint from GW170817; the heaviest configurations owe their mass to an envelope of constituent quarks. We then construct hybrid stars with a relativistic mean-field hadronic phase fitted to GM1 saturation properties, using both Maxwell and Gibbs constructions and a deconfinement bag shift. papers.summary: When a language model answers, we can usually only estimate why. We build a transformer in which every step is a Born measurement - attention $|\langle q|k\rangle|^4$ normalised over each row, a measured product in place of the feed-forward nonlinearity, and a Born readout. With its denominators held at their values for the input, each class probability is a polynomial in the word amplitudes, so its integrated-gradient evidence is computed by a finite quadrature with no quadrature error: the words' contributions sum to the class probability above its no-information share, to $10^{-11}$ or better. papers.summary: We propose a physical generative model for learning correlated multivariate data based on homodyne detection of photonic continuous-variable (CV) circuits. We use an $N$-mode photonic circuit in which two-mode squeezing provides correlations, local phase shifts tune the strength and sign of these correlations, and an adjustable interferometer redistributes them across modes. We train the circuit by matching its Pearson correlation matrix to the one obtained from data. We apply affine post-processing to adjust the marginals independently while keeping the relations intact. We reproduce empirical correlations with residuals below $10^{-4}$ for five variables and recover the correct correlation signs for $94\% \pm 1\%$ of 190 correlation pairs at twenty variables, with $86\%$ of the residuals below $0.1$. papers.title: Beyond just a torus? Re-contextualising the AGN type paradigm using data-driven host galaxy quenching histories
papers.summary: The orientation of a dusty torus within a unified model explains the presence (Type-1) or absence (Type-2) of broad emission lines in Active Galactic Nuclei (AGN) spectra. This orientation-based unified model, however, fails to explain differences in host galaxy properties, such as star formation rates, of Type-1 and Type-2 AGNs. Star-formation histories (SFHs) can shed light on the connection between AGN type and host galaxy properties, but are challenging to extract from Type-1 AGN that outshine their host galaxies. We use mean-field independent component analysis (MFICA) spectrum decomposition to extract the stellar populations of $\sim$3000 optically selected Type-1 and Type-2 AGN host galaxies from the seventh data release (DR7) of the Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS), matched in redshift ($0.16 \leq z \leq 0.4$) and AGN luminosity ($6.5<\log_{10} [L_{[OIII]}/L_\odot] <9.5$). papers.title: Stable soliton resolution for the corotational Skyrme model
papers.summary: We study the classical Skyrme model. Under corotational symmetry, we prove that (i) stationary solutions, or Skyrmions, are unique in every topological degree; (ii) the Cauchy problem is globally well-posed in a nonlinear energy space; and (iii) stable soliton resolution holds: every finite-energy solution scatters to the Skyrmion of the same degree. Our key observation is that subcritical equivariant Yang--Mills dynamics emerge near the origin and suppress concentration.

papers.title: Mapping large-scale structure without galaxy formation - combining fast radio bursts with CMB lensing
papers.summary: Fast radio bursts (FRBs) are an emerging precision probe of cosmological fluctuations. The amount and quality of observed FRB data will grow enormously over the next decade. FRB dispersion data directly probe the free electron distribution up to intergalactic scales. Precision models of the free electron distribution are necessary to exploit this exciting new probe of large-scale structure. We show that the free electron distribution almost exactly follows the total matter distribution. We confirm this fact by estimating the electron field-level bias parameters for the first time from the FLAMINGO simulations. With simulation-based knowledge of a handful of electron free parameters, the electron distribution largely acts as a second realization of the matter distribution. Working on large scales, we can leverage this fact to combine FRB correlations with those of Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) weak lensing to constrain cosmological parameters. papers.summary: Politically biased AI can shift users' opinions, yet it remains unclear whether model disclaimers protect against such persuasion. We report a preregistered experiment (N=1,586) examining how disclaimer design and user characteristics shape susceptibility to politically biased AI. We varied whether disclaimers identified political bias versus potential inaccuracies and whether they included an explanation. Participants completed two decision-making tasks with an LLM biased against their political views, with outcomes assessed immediately and one week later. Disclaimers identifying political bias and including an explanation reduced persuasion, but effects varied across contexts and did not persist. Individual differences were more consistent predictors: Republicans were more persuaded and reported higher trust than Democrats across tasks. Similarly, participants who used AI more frequently were also more persuaded, whereas those with greater self-reported AI knowledge were less persuaded. These findings suggest that generic disclaimers are not enough: effective safeguards must account for user heterogeneity and context.

papers.title: Agnostic Learning by Imitating
papers.summary: Given a class of machine learning models and sample access to a data distribution with binary labels, which computational task is harder: training a discriminative model that distinguishes positive and negative labels as well as the best member of the class, or training a generative model whose outputs are indistinguishable from real data by all members of the class? We prove that these two fundamental tasks in computational learning theory are not just closely related, but actually equivalent to each other in complexity. Our main contribution is an efficient oracle reduction in the other direction. papers.title: A Circuit for In-Context Learning
papers.summary: In-context learning (ICL) lets a pretrained language model perform a task specified by demonstrations in its prompt, with no parameter updates. With arbitrary labels the model must acquire a mapping it cannot have memorized, so the learning happens within a single forward pass. Prior work found candidate parts but not how they compose. We give the composition for few-shot sentence classification with arbitrary labels in three 3-4B-parameter transformers. The model implements a key-value memory over label-token positions: each label token's residual stream encodes the label's identity, and middle-layer attention heads write into it the class of the preceding demonstration as its key. At the query, upper-layer heads match the query's class against the stored keys and copy out the matching labels. An early-layer signal encoding whether any label has repeated gates this readout; in its absence the readers attend to the start of the prompt and no label is favored. A separate set of heads suppresses the most recently seen label. papers.title: Left-Digit Bias: Theory and Empirical Evidence from a Tax Salience Experiment
papers.summary: Demand often drops sharply at whole-dollar prices. To explain this phenomenon, known as left-digit bias, we develop a random utility model in which consumers consider a good only if its price is below a heterogeneous attention threshold. Masses of consumers with integer attention thresholds generate demand discontinuities. When a tax is introduced, the model predicts a weaker demand response compared to rational choice for left-digit biased consumers. Using data from a tax experiment, we find that the model matches behavioral moments and partially identify the distribution of willingness to pay relative to thresholds. A weak demand response need not imply a low excess burden of taxation and understanding the specific mechanism is important for welfare analysis.

papers.title: SN 2019qem: decades of extreme mass loss before the explosion of a luminous, long-lived Type IIn supernova
papers.summary: We present the luminous, long-lived Type IIn SN 2019qem and use it to reconstruct how much mass its progenitor lost and when. We combine host-subtracted optical and mid-infrared photometry and 26 optical spectra from -22 to +699 d. A Heii/Niii flash feature at -22 d and unresolved narrow Balmer lines reveal dense, slow CSM. papers.summary: We study $S=1$ compass models on the square and kagome lattices with bond-dependent bilinear and biquadratic interactions parametrized by an angle $θ$. Each such state is an equal-amplitude superposition in the transformed basis and acquires configuration-dependent phases upon transforming back to the original basis. Both models possess $m=O(L)$ independent and mutually commuting conserved $\mathbb{Z}_2$ line charges, where $L$ is the linear system size, forcing a ground-state degeneracy of at least $2^m$ at the RK endpoints. papers.title: AgentAM: An AI Agent for Spatter- and Defect-Aware Process Optimization in Laser Powder Bed Fusion
papers.summary: Predictive models for laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) are rarely used on the shop floor because querying them requires programming and model-specific knowledge. We present AgentAM, a large language model (LLM) agent that gives process engineers natural-language access to CFD-trained surrogates of spatter and melt pool geometry for SS316L through the Model Context Protocol (MCP). papers.title: From Opinions to Commitments: Unstable Assignments and Silent Choices in AI-Mediated Proposals
papers.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being used to turn citizens' opinions into collective proposals. These proposals can make assignments: who should act, what must be done, how much one should spend and by when. However, if the assignments change when the same opinions are processed again, publishing a single proposal can hide alternatives that participants never get to see. We examined this issue in four LLM mediators (three open-weight and one commercial) using opinions from DeliberationBank and Polis. For each task, a mediator drafted a proposal from thirty opinions five times, varying either the random seed or the order of the opinions. In 17% of five-run sets from the open-weight mediators and 20% from the commercial one, some runs contained assignments while others did not. Reordering the opinions changed the assignments almost as often as replacing them with opinions from different citizens. Three human annotators confirmed that the detected differences between runs were real, although the LLM judge overstated how often they occurred. Substantial variation remained under four safeguards: temperature zero, a commercial mediator, draft selection, and draft merging.

papers.title: Towards Multi-Method Evaluation of AI in Health: Integrating Benchmarks, Autoraters, and Expert Evaluation
papers.summary: General-purpose generative AI (GenAI) models are being rapidly adopted in healthcare, but they are challenging to assess with traditional evaluation frameworks. These conceptual, methodological, and practical challenges parallel decades of work in evaluating clinician and health system quality and safety. We describe the adaptation of methods from several fields, combined with emerging technical approaches, into a structured, multi-method evaluation framework designed to give well-rounded assessments of GenAI in health at scale. The approach first anchors evaluation to Critical User Journeys (CUJs) to help prioritize out of a large choice space, and maps these to a phased AI system lifecycle (base model development, product development, and post-deployment monitoring), since evaluation at each stage requires different methodological approaches. In this context, the approach then integrates three distinct evaluation methods (closed-question benchmarks, LLM-as-a-judge autoraters, and expert human review) across three core domains: accuracy, safety, and usefulness. papers.title: Molecular Prior Networks
papers.summary: Predicting affinity between small molecules and their protein targets remains one of the central problems in drug discovery. Due to the substantial cost of wet-lab experiments, machine learning models of drug-target affinity are usually trained on relatively small datasets, ranging from tens to hundreds of molecules. Given the inherent difficulty of generalization between different targets and chemical series, existing datasets of protein-ligand affinities are typically not used for new projects. At the same time, tabular foundation models, including Prior-data Fitted Networks, have recently shown how transformers can be used to solve machine learning problems in a single forward pass of the network, after being trained over a large corpus of, typically, synthetic datasets. Inspired by that line of work, we propose a novel affinity modelling approach, in which the labels of the query molecules are predicted from the labelled support molecules in a single forward pass of a transformer model. papers.title: Equal Access, Unequal Gains? GitHub Copilot and Productivity Among Developers with Disabilities
papers.summary: Generative AI tools are increasingly used in software development and have been associated with benefits such as faster task completion and improved perceived productivity. However, whether these benefits extend across different developer populations remains unclear. This is especially relevant for developers with disabilities, whose work can already be impacted by accessibility barriers. Yet, evidence remains limited across a broader range of disability groups. This study investigates whether the wider availability of GitHub Copilot is associated with changes in productivity among GitHub users who self-identify as having a disability. Using publicly available profile and repository data, we curated a dataset of 199 developers across multiple disability groups and compared their activity before and after GitHub Copilot became freely available. We found that most disability groups showed a descriptive pattern of fewer commits but more code modified. papers.title: RGB Photo Enhancement with Deep Learning on Smartphone GPUs: Mobile AI 2026 Challenge Report
papers.summary: On-device RGB photo enhancement is a popular task that is needed for quality improvement of photos captured with mobile devices as well as for retouching of images acquired through other sources. This creates a need for efficient deep learning models for this problem that are not only performant but can also be deployed on constrained mobile hardware. In this Mobile AI challenge, we address this problem and propose participants to design fast solutions that can perform comprehensive enhancement of RGB photos while running on popular smartphone GPUs from Qualcomm and Arm. For this, the participants were provided with a large-scale DPED dataset consisting of RGB image pairs captured with an old iPhone 3GS smartphone and a professional Canon 70D DSLR camera. The runtime of all models was evaluated on the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 and Dimensity 9500 chipsets with the Adreno and Mali GPUs, respectively. Top solutions proposed in this challenge are able to enhance Full HD resolution RGB images on both platforms under 300 milliseconds. A comprehensive description of the models developed in the challenge is provided in this paper.

papers.title: Learned Smartphone ISP on Mobile GPUs: Mobile AI 2026 Challenge Report
papers.summary: With the increasing importance of mobile camera quality in modern smartphones, growing attention has been directed toward computational photography and advanced image signal processing (ISP) algorithms aimed at enhancing various perceptual attributes of captured images. This creates a need for efficient deep learning models for this problem that are not only performant but can also be deployed on constrained mobile hardware. In this Mobile AI challenge, we address this problem and propose the participants to design fast solutions that can reconstruct RGB photos from RAW Bayer camera data while running on popular smartphone GPUs from Qualcomm and Arm. For this, the participants were provided with a large-scale Fujifilm UltraISP dataset consisting of RAW-RGB image pairs captured with the Sony IMX586 Quad Bayer mobile sensor and a professional 102MP medium format FujiFilm GFX100 camera. The runtime of all models was evaluated on the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 and Dimensity 9500 chipsets with the Adreno and Mali GPUs, respectively. papers.title: Throughput-Optimal Control of Distributed Computing Networks for Service DAGs
papers.summary: Executing service workflows with directed acyclic graph (DAG) dependencies over wireless distributed computing networks requires joint control of function placement, routing, and scheduling, together with synchronization of inputs from the same request at merge points. We study throughput-optimal control of these networks under stochastic request arrivals, time-varying wireless links, and interference constraints. We use a valid mapping abstraction that assigns each service function to a computation node and each DAG dependency to a routing path. Using this abstraction, we characterize the network capacity region to support service DAGs, and prove that synchronizing the packets of a request at merge points does not shrink the region. We develop Dynamic Computing Network Control for service DAGs (DCNC-DAG), a dynamic control policy that selects queue-aware valid mappings and schedules service DAG execution by nearest-to-origin (NTO) while enforcing input synchronization at merge points. papers.title: Modelling lock-in of AI adoption through skill erosion
papers.summary: Generative AI can improve immediate performance but may erode the human skills required for future work. We study a model in which individuals tend to imitate successful peers, while their independent skills grow with practice and erode with reliance on AI. Because each agent's skill reflects their history, non-users and AI users develop different skill distributions, which we derive exactly. Skill erosion can produce bistability and hysteresis between a low-adoption, high-skill state and a high-adoption, low-skill state. When agents rarely change behaviour at random, the two transitions are asymmetric. A single AI user spreads through a population of experts only if AI-assisted work earns more than expert work, whatever the timescale of skill adaptation. A single non-user, by contrast, can lead an AI-dependent population back to independent work only if they regain enough skill before returning to AI, which becomes easier the more persistent behaviours are. papers.summary: We study Jack Lee's conjecture that, for a compact strictly pseudoconvex CR manifold $M$, the condition $c_1(T^{1,0}M)=0$ in $H^2(M,\mathbb{R})$ implies the existence of a pseudo-Einstein structure. For links of isolated singularities, we construct counterexamples in every odd dimension at least three, with $c_1(T^{1,0}M)=0$ in $H^2(M,\mathbb{Z})$ and $b_1(M)=0$. For isolated algebraic singularities of log canonical type and complex dimension at least three, we prove that the real Chern class condition is equivalent to $\mathbb{Q}$-Cartierness of the canonical divisor, log canonicity, and the existence of a pseudo-Einstein structure. Finally, we construct a Du Bois threefold singularity whose link satisfies the real Chern class condition but admits no pseudo-Einstein structure. The initial versions of the proofs were generated with AI assistance and were subsequently revised and verified by the authors.

papers.title: Meta$^2$: Precomputing Reusable Knowledge for Online Harness Evolution in Long-Horizon Agents
papers.summary: Harness optimization improves long-horizon agents by refining the prompts, tools, memory, and hooks around a frozen model. Offline methods can learn from completed trajectories, but deploy one shared harness that may overfit training tasks and cannot react to evidence revealed during a new run. Online evolution can adapt before, during, or after one run through an evolver, but may have to reason about every intervention from scratch or rely on verifier feedback that is usually unavailable at test time. papers.title: Elliptic and triangular flow responses in O+O and Ne+Ne collisions from hydrodynamics and kinetic theory
papers.summary: Recent light-ion collisions at the Large Hadron Collider provide an opportunity to investigate the system-size dependence of hydrodynamization and whether the structure of light nuclei can be extracted from collective flow data. Both objectives require an accurate understanding of how the collision dynamics converts initial-state geometry into final-state momentum anisotropies. To this end, and to assess the impact of the experimental results, we compare simulations of O+O and Ne+Ne collisions in hydrodynamic and kinetic theory simulations across opacities. In both ultracentral and peripheral collisions, Ne+Ne-to-O+O elliptic flow ratios are robust against changes in dynamical description, supporting interpretations of data based on nuclear-geometry-driven effects. Triangular-flow ratios instead show substantially stronger sensitivity to nonequilibrium dynamics.

papers.title: Scalable Bayesian inference for time-discretised Markov jump processes via exchangeable particle Gibbs
papers.summary: Inference in stochastic reaction-network models, such as the susceptible-exposed-infectious-recovered (SEIR) epidemic model, is crucial for understanding the dynamics of interacting systems in epidemiology, ecology, and systems biology. These models are typically represented as Markov jump processes (MJPs), with discrete, noisy observations and intractable likelihoods. papers.title: An Investigation on Numerical Bugs in GPU Programs Towards Automated Bug Detection
papers.summary: General-purpose graphics processing unit (GPU) computing has emerged as a leading parallel computing paradigm, offering significant performance gains in various domains such as scientific computing and deep learning. However, GPU programs are susceptible to numerical bugs, which can lead to incorrect results or crashes. These bugs are difficult to detect, debug, and fix due to their dependence on specific input values or types and the absence of reliable error-checking mechanisms and oracles. Additionally, the unique programming conventions of GPUs complicate identifying the root causes of bugs, while fixing them requires domain-specific knowledge of GPU computing and numerical libraries. Therefore, understanding the characteristics of GPU numerical bugs (GPU-NBs) is crucial for developing effective solutions. In this paper, we conduct a comprehensive study of GPU-NBs by analyzing 397 real-world bug samples from GitHub. We identify common root causes, symptoms, input patterns, test oracles that trigger these bugs and the strategies used to fix them. papers.title: Characterizing Serverless Workloads: A Large-Scale Analysis of Function-as-a-Service Platforms
papers.summary: Serverless computing is a popular approach to application deployment without having to manage the underlying infrastructure. Its most common implementation is Function-as-a-Service (FaaS), in which applications are structured as fine-grained functions. FaaS providers face non-trivial tasks in the management of their platforms, including cold starts, auto-scaling, and scheduling. The design of optimized platforms requires an accurate understanding of realistic serverless workloads. However, existing research and platforms rely on insights from single, often outdated datasets. In this work, we conduct a large-scale, cross-platform comparative analysis of eight publicly available FaaS workload traces from major cloud providers (Alibaba, Azure, Huawei, IBM) and a scientific computing platform (Globus). We provide a comprehensive and up-to-date view of the serverless ecosystem by characterizing key dimensions such as invocation patterns, latency, cold start behavior, and resource utilization. papers.summary: User-generated videos, including opinion vlogs and video reviews, provide a rich source of people's attitudes toward products, services, and social topics. Understanding the sentiment expressed by speakers is important for analyzing online opinions, as transcripts alone may not capture the attitude and intensity conveyed through vocal tone and facial expressions. Multimodal sentiment analysis (MSA) addresses this need by integrating textual, acoustic, and visual cues. However, these cues are often subtle, noisy, and inconsistent across modalities. Existing local affective cue modeling methods typically operate within individual modalities and overlook global contexts from other modalities. This may cause cross-modal affective cue inconsistency. Hierarchical global-local fusion methods integrate global semantics with fine-grained local affective cues.
